title: Remove Duplicates from Sorted Array
prompt: Given an integer array `nums` sorted in non-decreasing order, remove the duplicates in place so that each unique element appears only once. The relative order of elements should be kept. Return `k`, the number of unique elements, after placing the first `k` elements of `nums` in sorted, deduplicated order (the rest of the array beyond `k` does not matter). You must do this in place using `O(1)` extra memory.

examples.explanation: The first two elements become [1,2]; k = 2.
The first five elements become [0,1,2,3,4]; k = 5.
When every element is the same value, only one unique element remains after deduplication, so k = 1.

constraints: nums is sorted in non-decreasing order
hints: Because it's sorted, every duplicate of a value sits directly next to it — you never need to search far to detect a repeat.
Use two pointers: one scanning the whole array, one marking the end of the deduplicated prefix built so far.
Only advance the write pointer and copy a value over when it differs from the last value kept, so duplicates get silently skipped.

solution.approach: Keep a slow pointer marking the boundary of the unique prefix built so far. Walk the array with a fast pointer; whenever nums[fast] differs from the last kept value (nums[slow - 1]), copy it into nums[slow] and advance slow. Sortedness guarantees all duplicates of a value are adjacent, so a single linear comparison against the last kept element is enough to detect and skip every repeat.
